chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya and Abdillah ibn Ja'far and Ahmad ibn Idris all from al-Husayn ibn 'Ubaydillah from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi 'Uthman from Abd al-Jabbar al-Nahawandi from Abu Ishaq from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Thuwair ibn Abi Fakhtah who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Husayn, whoever leaves his home intending to visit Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), if he is walking, Allah writes for him a good deed for every step and erases a bad deed with it, until he reaches the open field (al-Ha'ir); then Allah writes him among the successful ones. And when he completes his rituals, Allah writes him among the victorious ones. And when he intends to depart, an angel comes to him and says to him: I am the messenger of your Lord, Allah, conveying peace to you, and He says to you: Resume your deeds, for what has passed has been forgiven to you.'

key_terms.الْحَائِر: The open field or plain near the shrine
key_terms.مَنَاسِك: Rituals or rites of the visitation

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and blessings for visiting Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the profound spiritual merit of Ziyarat al-Husayn, framing it as a transformative act of worship where physical movement translates directly into divine recompense. The narrative underscores the concept of 'Istinaf al-'amal' (resuming worship) post-forgiveness, reflecting the Shia emphasis on continuous spiritual renewal and the intercessory status of the Ahl al-Bayt. This tradition serves as both a theological encouragement for pilgrimage and a practical reminder of the immediate spiritual benefits associated with honoring the Imam of the Age.
